notes:
I don't have any notes on Isaiah 28 for you yet, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

I sent requests to Enduring Word, three Bible Hub commentary pages (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary, plus Barnes) and Precept Austin. My code to read the replies broke before it could save any text. After that the tool stopped me from running anything else this turn, so I couldn't fix the problem or try again.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. With no pages read, writing notes now would mean filling them from my own memory. So I've written nothing rather than give you unsourced points.

If you ask me again, I'll start over and do the work in this order:
1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word; Bible Hub's Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Barnes and Benson pages; StudyLight; Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** probably vv. 11–12, which Paul quotes about tongues in 1 Corinthians 14:21, and v. 16, the cornerstone verse quoted in Romans 9–10 and 1 Peter 2. For these I'd look for each tradition's own teachers: GotQuestions, Sam Storms, the Assemblies of God (ag.org), Desiring God, GTY, Ligonier, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, and the LCMS.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, on the sound-play in vv. 10 and 13), and New Advent's Church Fathers for Catholic and Orthodox readings.
